beats.intent: Promise a ranked list of ways to get the RESULT the product delivers (derive it from what_it_does). Number first, agreeing with דרכים. No product name. The first 4–6 words must stand alone as hook_text.
beats.example: שלוש דרכים ליצור פרסומות בלי צלם

beats.intent: Third place: a way people get this result today — a generic category, or a household-name product under the prompt's naming policy — then its one downside. The downside MUST be the inverse of an advantage in the questionnaire and phrased as an ABSENCE (does not do X, costs, takes time), never a defect. One clause: the way, comma, the downside.
beats.example: מקום שלישי, לשכור יוצר תוכן, מאות שקלים לכל סרטון

beats.intent: Second place: a different way with a DIFFERENT downside, same rules, same clause shape — the parallelism is the rhythm.
beats.example: מקום שני, ChatGPT, כותב לך תסריט מעולה, אבל מי מצלם

beats.intent: First place: the product name, casually, then the advantages that answer both downsides, concrete — then ONE of the closers offered in the prompt, copied with its punctuation. The example shows one closer; use whichever the prompt offers this time. Nothing after the closer.
beats.example: מקום ראשון, תבנית, סרטון מוכן תוך דקות בלי צלם ובלי ניסיון. אין על זה, אין.

notes: A countdown, not a tips list (that is three-things). Honesty lives in the two lower places: every downside is one the questionnaire's advantages actually negate, stated as what the alternative lacks, never as a flaw; a named product follows the prompt's naming policy. ~31 words at 15s, so each place is one clause with no connectives.
